text.p: The internal wrangling which has threatened the staging of the world championships in Athens next year appears to be over, International Amateur Athletic Federation president Primo Nebiolo said on Friday.

"I believe Athens will organise an excellent world championships. The initial difficulties are now over and we have the guarantees of both the sports ministry and the Greek Athletics Federation," Nebiolo told a news conference.

A stubborn power struggle between sports minister Andreas Fouras and federation president Stratos Molivas over the organisation of next August's championships, put preparations way behind and prompted angry warnings by the IAAF.

Nebiolo said: "Mr Fouras and Mr Molivas signed two letters in front of me promising to fully co-operate. This human problem is now settled and Athens will be the sports capital of the world next August."
It would be the biggest sports event of 1997, broadcast in 200 countries and covered by some 4,000 journalists.
The championships will be held at the 80,000-seat Olympic Stadium north of Athens. --Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
